summary: Live audit playback fidelity check, correlation keys for SIEM ingest, and field-masking policy handover
description: Issue summary: Customer requests an on-demand fidelity check of live audit playback for a 30-minute window to validate that the SIEM ingest mapping preserves event ordering, correlation keys, and PII-masked fields. They also need a handover package documenting the applied field-masking rules (per-tenant) and a signed assertion that SSO events in the audit trail are complete for their legal hold. Impact: Potential regulatory gap if delivered artifacts cannot be used for e-discovery and incident reconstruction. Affects two mission-critical services that feed their SOC. Environment: Production tenant for ClearPay Financial (enterprise), region us-east. Desired deliverables: 1) a 30-minute sampled playback bundle (chronologically ordered) with resume tokens and correlation keys; 2) a manifest showing which fields were masked, the masking algorithm and key-rotation epoch; 3) signed assertion (HMAC) over replay manifest and a pointer to SSO assertion logs; 4) a short runbook for replay verification they can run in their SIEM.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer requests start_time = 2026-03-03T15:10:00Z, window = 00:30:00. 2) Run audited event export for tenant id 'clearpay-enterprise-01' with chronological ordering and include correlation_id header. 3) Verify that events with type 'sso.login' and 'sso.token_refresh' are present and not redacted beyond allowed pseudonymization. 4) Generate HMAC manifest using the current audit KEK and include rotation metadata.
logs: Relevant logs attached: audit-export-2026-03-03-window.log (excerpted), siem-mapping-validation.log. Console snapshots: replay-job-12345-timeline.png.
comments: 2026-03-05 16:12 - Aisha Kapoor: Customer provided legal hold reference LGL-2026-77 and asked for proof of SSO event completeness.
2026-03-05 16:45 - Support (Miguel Torres): Acknowledged. Started validation of export tooling; requested ETA for signed assertion.

2026-03-06 09:10 - SRE (Lina Schwartz): Found that the exporter can stream resume tokens but default masking removes entire 'user.email' field. Proposed approach: add pseudonymization token to manifest instead of full email.
2026-03-07 11:30 - Customer (ClearPay SOC): Confirmed they require reversible pseudonymization for emergency legal unredaction (escrow process) and asked for proof the key-holder process exists.
2026-03-08 14:05 - Security (Oliver Chen): Sent KMS attestation document and proposed HMAC signing using audit-signing-key-v3. Asked legal to confirm escrow steps.
investigation_notes: Initial exporter run produced out-of-order events when worker restart occurred; root cause: exporter partition assignment lost sequence token. A fix is available in exporter v2.4.1 (PR #8762) to persist sequence watermark to tenant metadata.

Masking policy audit: customer expects reversible pseudonymization for 'email' and 'phone.number' fields. Current prod masking uses irreversible hash for email. Need to schedule a controlled replay with escrow capability and documented access controls.

SSO completeness: cross-check between auth-service audit and audit-service shows 2 missing 'sso.token_refresh' events in the sampled window; likely due to short-lived TTL on auth audit buffer; retention config adjusted in staging for replay test.
resolution: In progress: SRE deployed exporter v2.4.1 to a canary in prod-us-east and re-ran the 30-minute export. The new run preserved ordering and emitted resume tokens. Security provided KMS attestation and we prepared a reversible pseudonymization plan using escrowed KEK with documented access controls. Customer approved a controlled handover meeting on 2026-03-10. Final artifacts to be delivered after legal sign-off and a scheduled replay verification session with ClearPay SOC.
